messages:
fergus: Heads up — canary in eu-west spiked during the v3 rollout. p95 went from ~200ms to ~5s around 11:12. Error rate bump to 3.8%. Canary tag: v3.0.0-canary-7. Anyone seeing the same?

deploy-bot: [alert] Canary health check failures exceeded threshold (3m window). Suggested action: consider rollback or pin traffic to v2.9.x. See /deploy status: https://deploy.redwood.internal/rollouts/3829 (automated) :rotating_light:

lina: Confirmed on my end — model-server logs showing repeated KV cache evictions + OOM spikes. First noticed at 11:10. This looks like a memory regression after the attention kernel change.

nate: If model-server OOMs, fallback to previous binary makes sense. Can we pin inference-api to v2.9.6 for all regions and stop further canaries?

amanda: I'm in favor of a fast manual rollback for canary and a config-level pin for prod until we validate fixes. We should also freeze change window for the rest of today.

eva: Support FYI — I'll draft a short customer note and update status page after we decide. We should avoid saying "rollback" until we have the exec decision.

srebot: Incident created: INC-2026-0457. SLA monitor triggered. Pager duty notify -> @oncall-sre.

maria: Ops checklist: 1) Pause canary rollout 2) Pin traffic 3) Revert model-server image OR deploy hotfix 4) Run smoke tests 5) Notify customers. Who has hand to execute 2 and 3?

fergus: I'm going to execute the pin and pause now. Command I'm running:```bash
# pause rollout and pin to v2.9.6
redwoodctl rollout pause inference-api --group eu-west
redwoodctl pin-version inference-api --region eu-west --version v2.9.6 --reason "canary instability"
# verify
redwoodctl rollout status inference-api --region eu-west
```

amanda: I'll take the revert if we need it. Ready to run:```bash
redwoodctl rollback inference-api --to-version v2.9.6 --region eu-west --force --notes "emergency revert — canary instability"
kubectl -n inference rollout status deploy/inference-api -w
```

lina: After pin, we should also throttle new inference requests and bump autoscaler min replicas to avoid cold-start spikes. Suggest: set minReplicas=6 for eu-west for 30m.

nate: Agree. Also enable KV-cache retention (config flag) so we don't thrash caches during the revert validation.

fergus: Done: paused canary and pinned EU to v2.9.6. CLI output: "rollout paused" / "pin applied". Rolling verification: 200 OK on healthcheck but p95 still at ~480ms briefly, dropping to ~210ms after replicas warmed.

eva: Draft sent to customers preview channel and support ops. Short note: "We detected elevated errors in a canary deploy of v3.0.0; traffic has been pinned to the prior stable release while we investigate. No user data impact expected. We'll follow up with next steps."

srebot: Pager duty status: Acknowledged by @maria and @amanda. Adding runbook tag: "rollback-criteria".

maria: Next steps: 1) Collect model-server heap dumps from canary instances 2) Run perf regression tests against v3 locally 3) If fix is trivial, can do a fast patch and re-canary. If not, open a postmortem. I'll own the heap dumps.

fergus: Thanks folks. Filing a short release note entry and marking the change window frozen until 20:00 UTC today. If anyone needs emergency exceptions ping me. (reacted :thumbsup:)

nate: Follow-up: schedule a tiny canary with kernel flag off and 5% traffic in 2 hours, if smoke passes we'll ramp.

lina: I'll attach logs/heap-dumps to INC-2026-0457.

amanda: Executed revert for global prod pinned route as a precaution. CLI: "pin applied to global-route, rollback queued". Monitoring for 10m.

fergus: Last check (11:28): error rate down to baseline, latency stable. Closing action: keep pin until regression is understood. We'll update this thread with postmortem link.

deploy-bot: Rollout event: pause confirmed. Pins: inference-api@eu-west -> v2.9.6, inference-api@global-route -> pinned. Links: https://deploy.redwood.internal/rollouts/3829 /incidents/INC-2026-0457

amanda: I'll draft the postmortem skeleton and start RCA notes.

eva: Customer note posted at 11:34.

fergus: End of thread — thanks everyone.
